name: Accordion
description: CSS accordion on native <details>: animated height (::details-content + interpolate-size), chevron or plus/minus, bordered, separated and card variants; optional <mv-accordion type="single">. Also covers Collapsible. A native disclosure group (WAI-ARIA Disclosure pattern), with optional headings in the triggers.

builder.summary: Expandable sections, one or several open

type.label: Open at once
type.help: Several sections open together, or only one at a time

data-variant.label: Style
data-variant.help: One outlined box, separate boxes, or filled tiles

data-icon.label: Indicator
data-icon.help: The sign that shows a section opens: arrow, plus, or none

name.label: Group name
name.help: Sections sharing this name close each other, one open at a time

useWhen: Secondary content must be tucked away so users can expand only the sections they care about
Several collapsible sections should allow only one open at a time, like a settings group or help panel
A single show-more toggle is needed around extra details, using the standalone collapsible
Hidden text must stay findable with in-page search and readable by crawlers

avoidWhen.when: A full marketing FAQ section with heading, index and contact note is needed
Users switch between parallel views of equal importance rather than expanding sections
The content is critical and must be seen by everyone; hiding it behind a toggle reduces its visibility
An audit requires the strict WAI-ARIA Accordion pattern (heading wrapping a button with aria-controls); this component is a native disclosure group

attributes.name: type
attributes.description: On <mv-accordion>: single allows only one open item (native name attribute set automatically, JS fallback).

attributes.name: data-variant
attributes.description: On .mv-accordion: a single outlined box, separate boxes, or filled tiles where the open item lifts.

attributes.name: data-icon
attributes.description: On .mv-accordion or an item: chevron on the right, plus that turns into minus, chevron before the label, or no indicator.

attributes.name: name
attributes.description: Native on <details>: same name = exclusive group, no JS.

attributes.name: data-value
attributes.description: On an item: value reported in mv-change (its index otherwise).

properties.name: value
properties.description: Values of the open items; assign it to open/close items programmatically.

events.name: mv-change
events.description: An item opened or closed. detail: { value: string[], item, open }. With type="single", opening an item also closes the open one: two events, one per item.

slots.name: details.mv-accordion-item > summary
slots.description: Trigger; optional leading <svg> icon. Wrap the label in a heading (<h3 class="mv-accordion-heading">, any level) for headings navigation; .mv-accordion-subtitle inside it gives a two-line header.

classes.name: mv-accordion-heading / -subtitle
classes.description: Title (a heading element, or a span) and subtitle inside the <summary>; a heading takes the trigger styles.

classes.name: mv-collapsible
classes.description: Collapsible: a standalone <details class="mv-collapsible">, same height animation, free-form <summary> (style it yourself, e.g. mv-button).

classes.name: mv-accordion-chevron
classes.description: On an <svg> inside a <summary>: rotates 180° on open.

a11y:
A group of native
/ disclosures (WAI-ARIA Disclosure pattern, the one the APG uses for FAQs), not the stricter APG Accordion pattern (heading wrapping a button, aria-controls). The browser exposes each as a toggle with its expanded state, kept in sync with open, name and in-page search; Enter and Space toggle, Tab moves between triggers. No arrow keys: they would stop the page from scrolling (removed from the APG accordion pattern in 2026). Put a heading in the trigger (

…

, level chosen for the page) so headings navigation finds each section: NVDA and VoiceOver list it; JAWS and TalkBack may not (2018-2021 tests). Do not add role, aria-expanded or aria-controls to , nor a role to
: the native semantics already carry them, and role="button" hides the heading and the state in Safari. Known limit: with the native marker hidden, some screen readers do not always announce the state change. Closed content is out of the accessibility tree and still findable with Ctrl+F (opens automatically). Reduced motion or no ::details-content: instant open.
